title: A non-round triangle can drill a square hole
body: Reuleaux triangles, arcs bulging from each corner, have the same width in every direction like a circle yet are not round; mounted eccentrically in a Watts drill they carve nearly square holes. Constant width is a property, roundness is a stronger claim. Barbier's theorem gives all such shapes the same perimeter, pi times width, cheekily including the circle.
